questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I was personally attracted by the citys history and learning the german language, which made Heidelberg an obvious choice.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was overall a great experience which a lot of exciting things to do, but it was a tough exam period with quite difficult exams. Furthermore the German Bureaucracy can drive you nuts.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was quite easy although maybe things in the to do list could have been clearer.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Not any assistance as far as i remember.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: The Universitys orientation didn't necessarily answer the most relevant questions and made a pathetic attempt at building social connections.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Through WG-gesucht it was relatively easy to find an apartment that had a great location although it also was quite expensive.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Be aware when searching for a place to live that some dorms are excluseviely for men with far right beliefs, so although they seem cheap it might not be the nicest place to live.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was pretty easy but the queue at the administration service can take some time.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I had to go to the student administration and register. After that i received at student ID card and that was pretty much it.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I am actually not sure-

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I were successful with registering for the classes i wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Just make sure you get it done - the people at the administration are there to help you.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I felt that it were at sometimes unstructured and unclear what part of the syllabus was being explained during lectures but the level was as high as my home institution.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: It was pretty tough and the style of exercise/tutor classes was much more selfdependent than in Copenhagen.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Not as much that i had to do, so i was much more reliant on my self making sure that i knew how to do certain exercises.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Industrial Organization
Advanced Macroeconomics
Development Economics
German Language course

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
It is nice to do the language course in september as it counts for 7,5 ECTS and makes the semester that starts in october a lot easier. I would also recommend Development Economics as i found it really exciting.

IO and ADV. MACRO were hard subjects

questions.answer: RUNDFUNK - the german tv service fee costs about 100 euros.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food seems a little cheaper which is nice. The same goes for books.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I used the unisport which costed 30 euros for a semester which was nice as there were so many opportunities for different kinds of sports.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Try UNI-Sport - great place to meet other students and have a laugh.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Its nice to go to paris which is only 3 hours away by train. Freiburg, Mannheim and Stuttgart are also cool cities close by. Otherwise go hiking.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy it is very much a like with the danish culture.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Go up and talk with people they're usually not that bad.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Nothing really

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I like that you are so polite.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Its great to have a bike
The food in the Menza(Cantine) is pretty cheap
Use the nature - it is unique

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Nothing that comes to mind

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Getting better at german and having a life in a different country

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Being away from home and at times missing home.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
